focus: Process errors (c) to (e) and the generated-artifact drift family (f), plus the changelog version collision (g)
noveltyJustification: Six new findings: the scratch namespace-collision mechanism behind (c), the committed regenerations behind (d), the unverifiable-process-step mechanism behind (e), the designed source/generated split behind (f), the retrieval-fixtures family, and the branch-local version mint behind (g).
keyQuestions: Q2: What mechanisms produced process errors (b) to (e): the validator parsing link-shaped task text, the reviewer wildcard rm, the committed regenerated scratch tree and the claims made before verification?
Q3: Why did the generated artifacts — the trigger index, the Hermes agent copies, the compiled-route manifests and the leaf manifests — drift and need orchestrator re-mints?
Q4: Why did a changelog version collision occur at merge when main and the branch both minted system-spec-kit v2.7.1.0?
answeredQuestions: Q2: What mechanisms produced process errors (b) to (e): the validator parsing link-shaped task text, the reviewer wildcard rm, the committed regenerated scratch tree and the claims made before verification?
Q3: Why did the generated artifacts — the trigger index, the Hermes agent copies, the compiled-route manifests and the leaf manifests — drift and need orchestrator re-mints?
Q4: Why did a changelog version collision occur at merge when main and the branch both minted system-spec-kit v2.7.1.0?
ruledOut: A version-reservation service or lock on changelog numbers - the collision is rare, both sides can read origin/main, and a reservation layer adds a dependency with no caller today
A scratch-lifecycle manager for packets - the convention exists; the missing piece is naming, not machinery
